dhp221:1: One should abandon anger, one should abandon conceit,
dhp221:3: without clinging to mind and bodily form,
dhp221:4: sufferings never do befall the one having no possessions.
dhp222:1: Whoever should hold back arisen anger just like a swerving chariot,
dhp222:3: that one I say is a charioteer, other people are just rein-holders.
dhp223:1: Through kindness one should overcome anger,
dhp223:2: through goodness one should overcome a lack of goodness,
dhp223:3: through gifts one should overcome stinginess,
dhp223:4: through truth (one should overcome) lying speech.
dhp224:1: One should speak out the truth, one should not get angry, when requested give, if only a little,
dhp224:3: through these three conditions one can go to the presence of the gods.
dhp225:4: having gone there they do not grieve.
dhp226:1: For those who are always wakeful,
dhp226:2: who train both by day and by night,
dhp226:4: the pollutants are laid to rest.
dhp227:1: This is something of old, Atula, this is not something of today:
dhp227:3: they blame the one who sits silently,
dhp227:4: they blame the one who talks a lot,
dhp227:5: they blame the one who talks in moderation,
dhp227:6: there is no one in the world not blamed.
dhp228:1: There was not and there will not be,
dhp228:2: and at present there is not found
dhp229:1: The one who, after being examined day by day,
dhp230:1: one who is like a golden coin,
dhp230:2: who is there worthy to blame him?
dhp230:3: That one is praised by the gods,
dhp230:4: and has been praised by the Brahmās too.
dhp231:1: One should guard against bodily anger,
dhp231:4: one should have good bodily conduct.
dhp232:1: One should guard against verbal anger,
dhp232:4: one should have good verbal conduct.
dhp233:1: One should guard against mental anger,
dhp233:4: one should have good mental conduct.
